newsitem.title: INDIA: Low industrial buying for Indian metals.
newsitem.headline: Low industrial buying for Indian metals.

text.p: Indian base metals were steady on Wednesday in a narrow price band on the local market, dealers said.
Industrial buying was at a low ebb and trading activity remained dull as major players kept away ahead of the presentation of the union budget on Friday.
Copper was steady at 12,800 rupees per quintal, zinc at 7,300 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal.

"Market sentiments however remained firm amid reports of rising global prices but trading was dull as traders were expecting that Indian government may reduce import duty on the base metals in the budget," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
Nickel was steady at the higher level of 37,400 rupees per quintal. It was up by 200 rupees per quintal on Tuesday.
Tin was available at the previous level of 34,100 rupees and aluminium at 7,250 rupees per quintal, but trading was nominal.
